title: Barnard's Star — the fastest-moving star in our sky
plain_result: This star is so bright that it saturates SPHEREx's detector, and our position measurement fails for it: from SPHEREx we get -5.0 ± 1.9″ and +5.6 ± 1.5″ per year, which disagrees with Gaia's -0.80″ and +10.36″. The picture of survey 1 minus survey 2 does show the star's light moving north, as Gaia predicts, but we do not turn that picture into a number.

evidence_links.text: Why it fails: What failed, item 13

method_note: Saturated pixels are masked, so the position rests on the star's outer light, which is not enough here.
